mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in liquidity and an increase in borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which often precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE increases > 0.5pp, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months indicates weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS declines for 3 months, or if the correlation between RSAFS changes and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases > 1%, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and 5-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signals disinflationary pressure, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate monetary easing.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL declines for 3 months, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL changes and 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 4%, it signals a strong demand for housing supported by low interest rates, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases > 10% and FEDFUNDS < 4%, or if the joint effect of HOUST and FEDFUNDS on 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) relative to its 12-month moving average suggests a robust supply side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average, or if the correlation between INDPRO levels and 5-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
